correctness.rationale: Reconstructed definitions and each lemma independently. The no-isolate assumption certifies all one-vertex deletions; the super domination threshold forbids deletion of three or more. For four blocks, the one nonsingleton block must join every coalition pair and the other three singleton complement-pairs are exactly edges of a triangle; converse holds. Three blocks exist whether the deletion graph is complete or not. For three blocks, at least two of the three remainders must be singleton or eligible pair. Double-count the three possible designated small pairs and subtract two when all three are small: only n=5 (two edges and singleton) or n=6 (three disjoint edges). This proves the binomial + (n−3)edges + 2-matching − exceptional correction identity. Independent brute-force implementation tested 2388 eligible graphs of orders 5,6,7; finite checks are corroboration, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper was inspected in full in accessible arXiv HTML. Its Theorem 3.2 implies the four-block ceiling in this regime but supplies neither equality characterization nor the exact number of three-/four-block partitions; its open Problem 7.1 explicitly asks for equality classification. Targeted published-finding corpus searches identified a stronger input result for complete multipartite super dominating sets, credited in the proof, but no published statement covering the general triangle/graph-matching theorem. Novelty is assessed only for this structural partition theorem, not for that input lemma or the universal ceiling.
residual_risks: The complete separately indexed multipartite paper was not inspected; a previously published hidden coalition specialization could overlap, although the general arbitrary-graph formula is not in its returned scientific summary.
Unindexed or unpublished equivalent results remain possible. Absence from search results is not proof of worldwide uniqueness.

value.rationale: A natural question left by the motivating Theorem 3.2 and Problem 7.1 is when the sharp upper bound on coalition blocks is attained. This result completely solves that equality question for every graph with super domination number at least n−2 and goes beyond the extremal value by enumerating all attaining partitions, plus all three-block partitions, through structurally canonical triangle/matching invariants. This is an infinite and graph-wide classification and a useful exact reduction, not an artificial finite slice or mere recomputation of a known table.
